paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Before God says one command, He says who He is: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery." (Exodus 20:2) He rescued them FIRST. So these commands come from the One who already carried them out, and He's not handing out rules to strangers.

Then look at what He asks: no other gods, no idols, honor His name, and keep the Sabbath because He made everything in six days and rested on the seventh (Exodus 20:11). Honor your father and mother, and don't murder, steal, lie or covet your neighbor's things. It all comes down to loving God and loving the people around you. I think that's why even the wanting gets a command (Exodus 20:17), because God cares about the heart, and not just the hands.

And the people trembled at the mountain and stood at a distance, then told Moses, "Speak to us yourself and we will listen… But do not let God speak to us, or we will die." (Exodus 20:19) Moses answers, "Do not be afraid… For God has come to test you, so that the fear of Him may be before you, to keep you from sinning." (Exodus 20:20) So the fear of God is a good thing here, friend, because it keeps you close to what He says. Hold on to your apron, because this teaching isn't done.
